Both link forms have been checked and work. The raw.githubusercontent.com links were fetched and returned 200, and the byte sizes exactly matched the catalogue. The via CDN links could not be checked from the environment in which this page was created — outbound access to cdn.jsdelivr.net is blocked there — so they are composed according to the documented jsDelivr URL form, and the owner manually checked one of them on 2026-09-20. Both are kept: one costs this project nothing, and a reader for whom one of them is unavailable still has the other.

IMPORTED COPY — this is not WHO and not a live site. This page was created by the {folioAssistant} tool on the basis of {iris}'s own catalogue, modelled by reference: {figures}. The WHO logo is deliberately omitted, and the generated covers are not shown for the same reason: the emblem from the publications is printed on them.
Imported replica. Created on the basis of {catalogue} using {generator}. Layout modelled on {iris}; every number on this page was read from the catalogue, not copied from a screenshot.

There is no Dublin Core record. The catalogue reports this rather than synthesizing metadata from the PDF: this is rule R8 of the iris-dspace skill, never derive metadata from the PDF if a record exists, the flip side of which is that a missing record stays missing.

This is the main entrance, not the library visualizer. The full library/ visualizer is task jbx2, and it is being created separately. This page reproduces the IRIS home page and leads onward, rather than becoming a second answer to the same question.

Three paths to one record — that is the point. The catalogue knows this record once; the bytes are available at the original source at WHO, here as a replica page and from a CDN node — jsDelivr serves any open repository, so the last path costs this project nothing for hosting. The knowledge graph says what exists and where; the CDN says nothing and simply serves the files.

Where the held copies actually reside — task yl5w. The catalogue gives for each of them the path uploads/<name>.pdf relative to who-iris/, and all three of these paths are missing: #477 moved library/ into this instance and left uploads/ in cat-harness/.

The main purpose of the Institutional Repository for Information Sharing (IRIS) is to provide free digital access to the scientific and technical publications of the World Health Organization (WHO), including materials of its country offices, regional offices and headquarters. In addition, IRIS covers the mandates established by the Organization's governing bodies jointly with its Member States.
